messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — we plan to rotate the infra service-account key in the 21:00 UTC change window. This will update the IAM key used by the deploy pipeline. Canary could fail if it lands mid-run.
Sam: How long is the deploybot canary window again?
Maya: Canary is 10m by default. If key swap hits during canary it fails auth and deploybot will auto-rollback.
Nina: Do we have a safe escape hatch? We should avoid a rollback during release cutover.
Maya: Proposal: schedule key rotation for after the release traffic cut, or temporarily pin the deploy job to the old key while we rotate and verify.
Julian: Pinning sounds safer. We can set an env var on the deploy job: DEPLOY_IAM_KEY_ID=<old-key-id> and then flip after rotation.
Sam: Can we also instruct deploy-bot to pause automatic rollback if canary fails due to auth, so we can triage?
Maya: I don't want to disable rollback broadly. Instead: set a targeted escape hatch — if deploybot sees error code 401 from sts assume key rotation and alert instead of immediate rollback for the canary.
Julian: That requires a tiny deploy-bot rule change. I can push a short-lived exception for this release.
deploy-bot: scheduled change: "credential-rotation-1765439876" created by Maya. Canary policy: rollback_on_any_failure=true
Nina: If we change deploy-bot policy, add an annotation to release notes and to the run: `manual-escaperope=true`. so ops knows why we delayed rollback.
Maya: Agreed. Release notes line: "Temporary canary rollback hold for credential rotation (ops flag)." I'll add.
Sam: Terraform plan snippet for the key rotation (for context):
```
resource "aws_iam_access_key" "infra_deploy" {
  user = "infra-deploy-bot"
  status = "Active" // replacing old key
}
```
Maya: We'll run `terraform apply` in the maintenance slot: 22:00 UTC if the release at 21:00 goes green. If not green, we postpone rotation.
Julian: Ops checklist: 1) Add DEPLOY_IAM_KEY_ID pin to canary job 2) Push deploy-bot exception (retain for 1h) 3) Run rotation 4) Validate canary auth 5) Update release notes and flip env var 6) Remove exception.
Nina: Who owns step 2?
Julian: I will own the deploy-bot exception.
Maya: I'll own the Terraform apply and release notes update.
Sam: If canary still fails after rotation, do we abort release or failover to previous AMI?
Maya: If failures persist beyond 2 retries and are auth-related, abort release and roll back to previous known-good. We call paging if we see errors after retries.
deploy-bot: note: when manual exception enabled, alerts will still be sent to #eng-oncall.
Nina: Ok — update the release notes fragment and the PR description so support and product know what's happening.
Maya: Done — added: "Temporary canary rollback hold for credential rotation; expect brief follow-up verification."
Sam: LGTM. I'll stand by for the apply window. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks — I'll post a final readiness msg 30m before apply.
Julian: I'll open the deploy-bot change and tag @eng-oncall for awareness.
Maya: ETA: rotation 22:00 UTC (if 21:00 release passes).
Sam: Copy that.
